classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied additive root relation to eliminate the root sum and pair product through all three coefficient equations, then apply positivity when dividing and choosing the parameter.

content.prompt: The cubic equation $x^3-Ax^2+6A=0$, where $A>0$, has roots $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\alpha+\beta$. Show that $A=4\sqrt3$.

answer.short: $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac A2$ and $\alpha\beta=-\dfrac{A^2}{4}$. The product of roots gives $-\dfrac{A^3}{8}=-6A$, so $A^2=48$. Since $A>0$, $A=4\sqrt3$.
answer.worked:
Sum of roots:
$$2\alpha+2\beta=A\qquad(1)$$
Sum of products of pairs of roots:
$$\alpha\beta+\beta(\alpha+\beta)+\alpha(\alpha+\beta)=0\qquad(2)$$
Product of roots:
$$\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)=-6A\qquad(3)$$
Rearranging (1) gives $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac A2$. Substituting into (2),
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha\beta+\beta\left(\frac A2\right)+\alpha\left(\frac A2\right)&=0\\\alpha\beta+\frac A2(\alpha+\beta)&=0\\\alpha\beta+\frac{A^2}{4}&=0\\\alpha\beta&=-\frac{A^2}{4}.\end{aligned}$$
Substituting $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$ into (3),
$$\begin{aligned}-\frac{A^2}{4}\left(\frac A2\right)&=-6A\\-\frac{A^3}{8}&=-6A\\A^2&=48,\end{aligned}$$
where division by $A$ is valid because $A>0$. Taking the positive root,
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\sqrt{48}\\&=4\sqrt3.\end{aligned}$$
